newsitem.title: ANGOLA: PETROFINA TARGETS 23,000 BPD IN ANGOLA'S SOYO.
newsitem.headline: PETROFINA TARGETS 23,000 BPD IN ANGOLA'S SOYO.

text.p: Belgium's PetroFina SA has restored most of its war-damaged base in Angola's northern port city of Soyo where it aims to increase production to around 23,000 barrels per day (bpd), a company official said on Monday.
"We are slowly getting back to our 1993 levels," Director General of Fina Petroleus de Angola, Carlos Alves, told Reuters.
"We are currently producing around 15,000 bpd but we should be able to reach 23,000 bpd by the end of the year. This will get us back to where we were when we had to abandon the fields," he added.

PetroFina abandoned its oilfields at Soyo near the Zairean border in 1993 when former rebel UNITA forces took control of the city from government forces. The fight for occupation of Soyo caused severe damage to oil installations, estimated at between $50 million to $60 million.

"Everything was damaged. The storage tanks were burned, the warehouses, the housing for the employees, basically all the infrastructure. We were lucky that only three or four well heads were damaged by explosives," Alves said.
He said the bulk of work to rebuild PetroFina's base at Soyo had been completed except for some smaller fields where damage still had to be assessed.
"We don't think there will be much more expense involved," Alves said.
Before reconstruction could begin the area had to be cleared of landmines.

Alves estimates the company will spend around $50 million on rehabilitating the area, but has no plans to rebuild two 70,000 cubic metre tanks, destroyed in the fighting in 1993. Instead, PetroFina is pumping oil to offshore holding facilities run by U.S.-based Texaco Inc in Block Two.

PetroFina has operated in Angola since 1954 and has worked in the oilfields around Soyo since 1969. The Soyo facilities are owned by the state oil company Sonangol which has a 51 percent share and Texaco.
Besides its base at Soyo, PetroFina also pumps from smaller onshore fields south of Luanda which produce around 2,000 bpd.
The company also runs the country's only oil refinery together with Sonangol as a minority shareholder, treating about 35,000 bpd, Alves said.
